## Verdict

**Kelp** costs least for a team of 8, at **$168 per month**. It carries the highest per-seat rate on the list ($21) but the only minimum that falls below the team size, so the team pays for exactly 8 seats. Acme Desk and Fennel HQ have cheaper headline rates but force payment for 20 and 40 seats respectively.

## Vendor pricing

| Vendor | Price per seat | Minimum seats |
|---|---|---|
| Acme Desk | $11 | 20 |
| Fennel HQ | $15 | 40 |
| Kelp | $21 | 1 |

## Cost at this size

Seats paid for = the greater of 8 (team size) or the vendor minimum.

- **Kelp:** minimum 1 < 8, so 8 seats paid. 8 × $21 = **$168 per month**. Effective rate $21.00 per person.
- **Acme Desk:** minimum 20 > 8, so 20 seats paid. 20 × $11 = **$220 per month**. Effective rate $27.50 per person ($220 ÷ 8); 12 unused seats worth $132.
- **Fennel HQ:** minimum 40 > 8, so 40 seats paid. 40 × $15 = **$600 per month**. Effective rate $75.00 per person ($600 ÷ 8); 32 unused seats worth $480.

Kelp is $52 per month cheaper than Acme Desk ($624 per year) and $432 per month cheaper than Fennel HQ ($5,184 per year).

## Risks

This result is fragile to growth, more so than in most comparisons here. Kelp wins only because of the minimums, not its rate. Acme Desk's $220 floor holds until 20 seats, and at 11 people Acme Desk ($220) and Kelp ($231) cross over — past 11 people Acme Desk is cheaper, and the gap widens at every seat above that. Fennel HQ's $600 floor holds to 40 seats and beats Kelp from roughly 29 people onward. If the team is likely to grow beyond ten or eleven, re-run these figures before committing.

The price list gives per-seat rates and minimums only. Feature sets, support tiers, usage limits and security posture are not stated, so this is a price ranking and not a value judgement. Annual commitments, discounts and onboarding fees are not on the list. Confirm whether minimums bind at signup or only at renewal.
